title: Session-bounded ingest contract to guarantee single-billing on at-least-once delivery
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Customers observe duplicate token charges when client libraries retry requests after timeouts or transient network failures. Existing dedupe tokens are effective for single-request retries but do not cover long-lived sessions where clients resume or reconnect and re-send request batches. Goal: design and implement a session-bounded ingest contract that allows at-least-once delivery for reliability while ensuring deterministic single-billing semantics across reconnects and client restarts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) For a given session_id and monotonic session nonce range, the platform must charge at most once for each logical request id even across client reconnects
2) Clients can resume a session after a client crash and replay inflight requests without risk of double-billing for already-committed usage
3) System gracefully handles clock skew and limited out-of-order monotonic counters from clients with a bounded replay window
4) End-to-end latency/regression: median request path adds <= 2ms and p99 <= 5ms overhead compared to current ingest path
5) Storage overhead for tombstones/leases remains under 1% of ingest storage budget at expected customer workloads (target numbers validated on staging)
6) Automated tests that simulate cross-region reconnects, duplicate delivery, and long retry tails, and assertions that billing ledger increments only once per logical id
design_notes: We introduce an explicit session contract: client sends session_id + session_epoch + request_seq (monotonic). Server allocates an ephemeral session lease and maintains a per-session provisional ledger for uncommitted seq ranges.

Upon first receipt of seq N, server writes a provisional entry (not charged) and replies with receipt token. Finalization paths: (a) explicit commit from client after successful processing, or (b) server-side idempotent commit after processing finishes. Only commit flips provisional to charged.

To limit state growth we use a hybrid approach: short-term in-memory lease for hot sessions + bounded persistent tombstones for last committed seq per session. A background GC sweep reclaims sessions with no activity after lease TTL + grace window.

Trade-offs: provisional ledger increases write amplification versus existing stateless dedupe. Pros: robust to client reconnects and partial replay; deterministic accounting. Cons: additional storage and GC complexity; needs strong testing around lease expiry races and cross-region failover.

Security: session tokens are bearer-like and must be scoped and rotated; KMS integration required for session signing in Private deployments. Security review flagged replay windows—mitigation: TTL + monotonic counters and server-side rate limit on session recreation.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike, 3d): prototype session lease component and provisional ledger in staging runtime; evaluate latency and storage; produce perf numbers and GC policy proposals (owner: Miguel)

Phase 2 (Core dev, 2w): implement session-lease API in ingest gateway, provisional ledger writes to existing billing store with new column flags; add commit/rollback operations; add metrics for provisional vs committed counts (owner: billing team)
Phase 3 (Integrations, 1w): update Go/Python SDKs to attach session metadata and expose helper retries that obey session contract; update rate limiter to be session-aware (owner: SDK & rate-limiting)
Phase 4 (Canary, 1w): deploy to canary accounts with synthetic workloads that exercise reconnect/replay patterns; run billing reconciliation against ground truth harness (owner: SRE + Billing)
Phase 5 (Rollout, 1w): gradual rollout with toggle flags; monitor alerts and dashboards; rollback plan available (owner: release engineer)
risks: Lease expiry race: client long-tail offline then resumes after TTL -> risk of double provisional creation if session_id reused. Mitigation: include session_epoch and server-side monotonic session lease id stored persistently at commit time.
GC correctness: premature tombstone removal could allow duplicate commits. Mitigation: conservative default TTLs, metrics to tune GC frequency, and a reconciliation sweep that detects anomalies.
Storage amplification: provisional entries increase billing store writes. Mitigation: compact provisional entries into session fingerprints and expire aggressively after commit.
Operational complexity: new stateful runtime surface increases blast radius on deploy. Mitigation: feature flag gating, incremental rollout, and thorough chaos tests.

SDK adoption: older clients not upgraded could bypass session semantics. Mitigation: retrofittable server-side heuristics fallback to existing dedupe tokens for backward compatibility and migration telemetry
testing_plan: Unit tests for session lease life-cycle and provisional->committed transitions
Integration tests: multi-client replay, cross-region reconnect, clock skew scenarios (simulate variable client clocks)
Stress tests: long running sessions with high seq churn to measure tombstone growth and GC effectiveness
Billing reconciliation job: compare committed ledger against expected counts from deterministic replay harness (automated nightly job)
Chaos test: force primary ingest node restart during commit window and assert no double-charge on replays
